runs.question: The filler drive keeps tripping on overcurrent at shift start. Can it wait until the planned stop?

outputs.answer:
[diagnostics]
Power wobble (DC-bus ripple) has risen from 1.9% to 5.8%, exceeding the 3% alarm limit, while DC bus voltage has drifted slightly down and IGBT temperature has climbed from 61°C to 79°C toward the 85°C alarm — all trending together over the 14-day window, not flat. Overcurrent trips are increasing in step (0→1→4) and cluster at shift-start acceleration, consistent with degraded DC-link capacitors that can no longer smooth the bus during high-current inrush, causing ripple-driven overcurrent trips and added IGBT heating. No prior capacitor work is on record (only a fan replacement and firmware update), so this is a first occurrence of aging power-smoothing components rather than a repeat fault. This pattern matches capacitor wear, not imbalance (no vibration data implicated) or cavitation (not a pump).

MACHINE: FILLER
FAULT_CODE: CAPACITOR-WEAR

[documentation]
Per MAN-FILLER-9.3 (DC-bus capacitor bank service), the manual states that ripple above 3% of nominal indicates capacitor ageing — matching the observed rise from 1.9% to 5.8%, which exceeds this alarm limit. The procedure calls for isolating the drive, waiting 15 minutes for bus discharge, and verifying voltage below 50 V before any contact with the capacitor bank. The bank must be replaced as a complete set using kit CAP-FILLER-KIT, as the manual warns that mixed-age capacitors will fail early. This is listed as a 3-hour job for one technician with the drive isolated. No separate run/no-run current or IGBT-temperature threshold procedure was found in the manual for this fault code.

SECTION: MAN-FILLER-9.3

[maintenance]
The ripple has exceeded the manual's 3% ageing threshold (5.8% vs. limit), confirming capacitor degradation as the root cause of the overcurrent fault, but the manual gives no run/no-run current or IGBT-temperature criterion tying this fault code to an immediate shutdown requirement. CAP-FILLER-KIT is out of stock (0 on hand) with a 21-day lead time, so replacement cannot happen at the next planned stop unless one is more than 3 weeks out — order the kit immediately regardless. Since the filler is the choke point of Line 3 (nothing downstream runs if it stops) and no documented run/no-run limit forces an immediate trip, the filler can continue running under close monitoring of ripple/current trend until the kit arrives, at which point the 3-hour isolated-drive replacement should be scheduled. Do not mix old and new capacitors per manual warning; replace as a complete set once parts are on hand. If ripple continues rising or overcurrent trips recur/worsen before the kit arrives, escalate to immediate shutdown regardless of parts status.
